risks.risk: TV size/model is unclear; scrap value depends heavily on screen size and panel type.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the back label showing model number and screen size (inches).
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest scrap/faulty TV end (worst case: smallest/least valuable panel).

risks.risk: Fault type unknown (e.g., panel damage vs power supply vs mainboard). Some faults are cheaper to repair than others, affecting scrap/parts value.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video showing power-on behavior (logo/boot attempt) and whether there is sound/backlight.
risks.if_unproven: Assume worst-case for parts: treat as non-repairable for buyer (scrap/parts only).

risks.risk: Missing accessories/stand/remote can reduce parts value.
risks.proof: Ask for photos of what comes with it (remote, stand/base, power cable) laid out.
risks.if_unproven: Assume minimal/no accessories included; price as bare TV for parts.

risks.risk: Physical damage (cracked screen, broken bezel) not clearly visible in the single photo.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the screen corners and bezel from multiple angles.
risks.if_unproven: Assume possible damage; keep pricing at the lowest scrap end.

proof_requests: Back-label photo showing exact LG model number and screen size (inches).
Short power-on video: show boot attempt/logo, whether there is sound, and whether backlight works.
Close-up photos of screen (corners/edges) and bezel for cracks or impact damage.
Photos of included items: remote, stand/base, and power cable.
response.reason: The photo shows an older LG flat-screen TV with a blank/non-working display, consistent with scrap/parts. However, model/size and fault type are not readable, so it must be priced at the worst-case scrap value using the closest cheapest comparable for faulty LG TVs.
